mismatched.name: waco crepes
mismatched.text: Reviewers across platforms consistently describe the staff as kind, helpful and attentive to allergies and dietary needs.

mismatched.name: SINLESS CAFÉ / Sinless Lab
mismatched.text: This is a sweets-focused bakery and café (canelés, cakes, puddings, cookies, afternoon tea), not a savory shokudo. No soy-sauce-based dishes are documented; if any savory items are added, ask whether wheat-free (gluten-free) soy sauce is used, since most Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.

mismatched.name: 都松庵 (Toshoan)
mismatched.text: Vegan options are limited. While the menu is built on plant-based red bean paste, many signature items contain dairy, including the An de cheesecake (cream cheese) and pancakes/treats served with butter or cream. Vegan diners should confirm which specific items are dairy-free before ordering.

mismatched.name: Smoothie etc
mismatched.text: Nuts are used heavily across the menu - nut milks, walnut and granola smoothie-bowl toppings, and nut-studded muffins - so anyone with a nut allergy should be explicit with staff and exercise strong caution.

mismatched.name: Pelgag
mismatched.text: Several menu items are wheat-based or fried (falafel balls, fried tempeh and vegetables, noodle dishes), so a strictly gluten-free meal is not something the sources confirm.

mismatched.name: Nicot & Mum's (vegan donuts)
mismatched.text: All doughnut dough is made without eggs and without dairy, using natural yeast and rice koji, so the doughnuts are suitable for vegan diners. This is core to the shop's recipe rather than a special-request item.

mismatched.name: KYOTO ENGINE RAMEN
mismatched.text: Some reviewers caution that staff are not always certain about every ingredient, so confirm specific allergen concerns directly.

mismatched.name: Wagyu Steak & Hamburger (Halal/Vegan/GF) – Arashiyama
mismatched.text: Vegan and vegetarian options are offered alongside meat dishes, but the kitchen is shared with wagyu and other animal products, so strict vegans should expect possible cross-contact and confirm preparation with staff.

mismatched.name: Falafel Garden
mismatched.text: The owner speaks fluent English and there is a picture menu, which makes discussing dietary needs and allergies much easier for international diners.

mismatched.name: Rin Halal Japanese & Vegetarian
mismatched.text: This is a Kyoto-style izakaya whose signature dish is a wagyu offal hot pot (horumon nabe) built on a white-miso broth. Miso, broth seasonings, and izakaya cooking like this almost always involve wheat-containing ingredients and shared pots and surfaces, so it should not be considered celiac-safe. Confirm every ingredient directly with the kitchen before relying on it.

mismatched.name: CoCo Ichibanya – Enmachi (near Nijo)
mismatched.text: The company openly states that contamination can occur both in the factory and in-store through shared equipment, utensils, and hand contact during cooking. The standard menu is not prepared in a celiac-safe environment.

mismatched.name: MOS & CAFE – Nijo Station
mismatched.text: MOS publishes an English allergen list (PDF) and notes that ingredients can vary by store and that information is not fully guaranteed, so celiac diners should rely on the sealed low-allergen items rather than the standard menu.

mismatched.name: MOS & CAFE – Nijo Station
mismatched.text: A vegetable burger (MOS Yasai Burger) is on the menu, but it is not certified vegan and is prepared in a shared kitchen alongside meat and dairy items; standard sauces and buns may contain egg, milk or animal-derived ingredients. Vegans should ask staff to check ingredients and preparation.

mismatched.name: Kura Sushi Plus – Kawaramachi (downtown)
mismatched.text: This is a conveyor-belt (kaiten-zushi) restaurant, so plates of many different items pass continuously over your seat. That open belt creates real potential for cross-contact, so it is best treated as manageable for non-celiac gluten-avoiders rather than celiac-safe.

mismatched.name: Kura Sushi Plus – Kawaramachi (downtown)
mismatched.text: The chain's founding principle is to avoid four common additives, MSG, artificial sweeteners, synthetic coloring, and artificial preservatives, drawing flavor from kombu and bonito instead, which appeals to diners watching what goes into their food.

mismatched.name: Kura Sushi – Teramachi
mismatched.text: Dishes are made under the company's 'Muten' policy without MSG, artificial sweeteners, synthetic coloring or artificial preservatives - useful for diners avoiding those additives (note: this is separate from gluten/allergen safety).

mismatched.name: Sushiro – Kawaramachi Takoyakushi
mismatched.text: Sushiro's own allergen guidance states that ingredients are handled in factories and stores alongside other allergens, so cross-contact is possible even when an item's recipe does not list wheat. As conveyor-belt sushi prepared in a shared kitchen with wheat-containing items, this location is not celiac-safe.

mismatched.name: Sushiro – Kawaramachi Takoyakushi
mismatched.text: The plain sushi rice and most plain fish nigiri (such as salmon, tuna, and shrimp) without sauce are not made with wheat, but they are prepared in an environment shared with wheat-containing products.

mismatched.name: Sushiro – Kawaramachi Takoyakushi
mismatched.text: The standard soy sauce provided at the table is brewed from soybeans and wheat, so it contains gluten. Celiac and gluten-free diners should bring their own tamari or gluten-free soy sauce, as the restaurant is unlikely to stock it.

mismatched.name: Sushiro – Kawaramachi Takoyakushi
mismatched.text: Sushiro publishes a detailed, regularly updated allergen chart covering the legally specified allergens plus additional recommended ones, marked per menu item, which lets diners check ingredients before ordering.

mismatched.name: ラーメン親爺 (Ramen Oyaji)
mismatched.text: This is a traditional wheat-noodle ramen shop. The noodles are wheat-based and the signature soup is a soy-sauce broth, so a standard bowl is not gluten-free and is not safe for celiacs. No gluten-free option is documented.

mismatched.name: 餃子屋もり (Gyoza-ya Mori)
mismatched.text: This is not a celiac-safe restaurant. The house specialty is gyoza, and standard gyoza wrappers are made from wheat flour; no gluten-free wrapper or dedicated gluten-free preparation is documented.

mismatched.name: 焼鳥 雷 本店 (Yakitori Kaminari – Honten)
mismatched.text: The standard tare sauce used to baste skewers is soy-sauce based, and most Japanese soy sauce contains wheat. Salt-grilled (shio) skewers avoid the tare entirely and are the safer choice, but should still be confirmed with the grill master, who prepares everything himself.

mismatched.name: 京料理 万長 (Kyoto Cuisine Mancho)
mismatched.text: As with most Japanese kitchens, the soy sauce used here can be expected to contain wheat, and it features across the seasonal dishes. Diners avoiding gluten should treat the menu as containing wheat unless staff confirm otherwise.

mismatched.name: キコク食堂 (Kikoku Shokudō)
mismatched.text: Cutlets are hand-breaded with fine breadcrumbs at the counter, confirming wheat coating on the fried items.

mismatched.name: 大國屋鰻兵衞 (Ōkuniya Manbei)
mismatched.text: The parent shop's river-fish products are explicitly described as simmered in soy and mirin (tsukudani), and the eel is grilled with a 'secret sauce' — consistent with a wheat-containing soy/mirin base throughout the house's cooking.

mismatched.name: 松乃家 (Matsunoya)
mismatched.text: Even the rice-bowl dishes are not gluten-free: the katsudon's egg-and-onion binding sauce is a dashi-and-soy-based broth, and the cutlet itself is wheat-breaded.

mismatched.name: 松乃家 (Matsunoya)
mismatched.text: The katsudon, donburi, udon and soba here all rely on soy-and-dashi-based sauces and broths. As with virtually all Japanese shokudo, the soy sauce almost certainly contains wheat, so these dishes should be treated as containing gluten.

mismatched.name: 手打ち蕎麦 かね井 (Teuchi Soba Kanei)
mismatched.text: The noodles themselves are self-milled 100% buckwheat with no wheat flour blended into the dough, so the buckwheat base is unusually pure compared with typical blended (nihachi) soba.

mismatched.name: 喫茶チロル (Kissa Tyrol)
mismatched.text: Japanese-style dishes here (e.g., teriyaki pork rice bowl, fried rice, hayashi rice) rely on standard seasonings; most Japanese soy sauce and Worcestershire-style sauces contain wheat, so these should be considered to contain gluten unless the shop confirms otherwise.

mismatched.name: 喫茶 KANO (Kissa KANO)
mismatched.text: Signature items center on white bread (the tamago sando on fluffy bread, toast with the morning set), so wheat is unavoidable in the headline dishes.

mismatched.name: 鉄板 みつ喜 (Teppan Mitsuki)
mismatched.text: Okonomiyaki and yakisoba here are built on a wheat-flour batter (also containing yam) and cooked on a shared teppan griddle alongside other wheat-based dishes, so cross-contact with gluten is effectively unavoidable. This is not celiac-safe.

mismatched.name: 鉄板 みつ喜 (Teppan Mitsuki)
mismatched.text: The signature okonomiyaki is steam-grilled directly on the same griddle used for all dishes; there is no indication of any gluten-free preparation area or accommodation.

mismatched.name: へんこつ (Henkotsu)
mismatched.text: This is not a celiac-safe restaurant. The entire menu centers on beef tendon and oxtail simmered in a hatcho-miso (fermented soybean) broth served as miso-nikomi oden -- a wheat/soy/dashi-heavy style. Oden items commonly contain wheat, and everything cooks in one large shared simmering pot, so cross-contamination is inherent and unavoidable.

mismatched.name: おいと (Oito)
mismatched.text: The oden broth is dashi/soy-based. Most Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat, so the broth itself should be treated as containing gluten.

mismatched.name: 和ダイニング なかぎし (Wa Dining Nakagishi)
mismatched.text: The master is known for being unusually warm and welcoming for Gion, including to first-time and solo visitors, so it is worth speaking to him directly about what you can and cannot eat — though no gluten-free or vegan accommodation is documented.

mismatched.name: 三平 (Sanpei)
mismatched.text: This is a tonkatsu specialist: the core dish is pork coated in wheat flour and panko (wheat breadcrumbs) and deep-fried. The same shared oil is used for breaded items such as cream croquettes and potato croquettes, so the fryer is not gluten-free. There is no indication of any gluten-free or celiac-safe preparation.

mismatched.name: かつ善 (Katsuzen)
mismatched.text: The kitchen is consistently praised as exceptionally clean and meticulous, with each cutlet prepared and fried fresh to order — good for general food hygiene, though not a substitute for allergen control.

mismatched.name: とんかつ清水 (Tonkatsu Shimizu)
mismatched.text: The cutlets are heavily dipped in tonkatsu sauce, and the izakaya menu is sauce- and soy-based; most Japanese soy sauce and tonkatsu sauce contain wheat, so these are not safe for wheat or gluten avoidance.

mismatched.name: ますや (Masuya)
mismatched.text: This is a from-scratch Showa-era yoshoku diner whose core dishes are built on wheat: hamburg steak with a flour-thickened demi-glace, hand-breaded fried shrimp and white-fish fry (the panko is reportedly made in-house), Napolitan spaghetti, pork piccata and ketchup-rice omurice. Gluten is structural to the menu, not an occasional ingredient.

mismatched.name: キッチンパパ (Kitchen Papa)
mismatched.text: Japanese yoshoku seasoning here leans on soy-based sauces and dashi; one documented special is an avocado hamburger steak with wasabi soy sauce. Standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, so soy-seasoned dishes should be treated as containing both soy and wheat.

mismatched.name: キッチンパパ (Kitchen Papa)
mismatched.text: Rice is freshly milled in-house each day and plain white rice is served with free refills, which can be a naturally gluten-free, low-allergen staple if prepared and served separately from sauced dishes (confirm with staff).

mismatched.name: お福 (Ofuku)
mismatched.text: A guest with celiac disease should avoid this shop; no gluten-free preparation or accommodation is indicated anywhere in the sources.

mismatched.name: やきとり雷 円町店 (Yakitori Kaminari – Enmachi)
mismatched.text: The tare (basting glaze) on yakitori is a soy-sauce-based sauce, and standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat. Tare-glazed skewers should be treated as containing wheat. No wheat-free soy sauce is documented here.

mismatched.name: やきとり雷 円町店 (Yakitori Kaminari – Enmachi)
mismatched.text: Salt-grilled (shio) skewers are seasoned only with Hakata salt rather than the wheat-containing tare, so the seasoning itself is wheat-free - but they share the grill with tare skewers, so this does not make them celiac-safe. Confirm directly with staff.

mismatched.name: 六曜社 地下店 (Rokuyosha Chikaten (Rokuyosha Basement S)
mismatched.text: This is a traditional kissaten whose signature item is a homemade wheat-flour donut made fresh on-site daily. Wheat baking and frying happen in a small shared space, so a strict celiac cannot be assured of a gluten-free experience here. Coffee itself is naturally gluten-free, but cross-contamination from the donuts cannot be ruled out.

mismatched.name: 六曜社 地下店 (Rokuyosha Chikaten (Rokuyosha Basement S)
mismatched.text: Coffee is brewed plain, one cup at a time, and ordered black it contains no gluten ingredients.

mismatched.name: からす (Karasu)
mismatched.text: The finishing sauces blend Kyoto, Osaka, and Hiroshima okonomiyaki sauces, which are soy- and wheat-containing; most Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat.

mismatched.name: からす (Karasu)
mismatched.text: Spicy items such as the beef-tendon suji-yaki use a doubanjiang and yanyanjiang (chili-bean paste) blend, which commonly contains soy and wheat.

mismatched.name: よりみち (Yorimichi (Okonomiyaki Yorimichi))
mismatched.text: The signature dishes (manbo-yaki, beta-yaki, hoso-yaki) are built on a wheat-flour batter and frequently include wheat noodles (soba-iri).

mismatched.name: 京都 下町のお好み焼き 昌・べた焼きの専門店 (Kyoto Shitamachi no Okonomiyaki Masa (Be)
mismatched.text: This is a betayaki (Kyoto-style okonomiyaki) specialist. The core dish is built on a wheat-flour batter cooked on a shared griddle (teppan), so it is not celiac-safe. Gluten is central to virtually every dish here.

mismatched.name: 京都 下町のお好み焼き 昌・べた焼きの専門店 (Kyoto Shitamachi no Okonomiyaki Masa (Be)
mismatched.text: Everything is cooked together on a single shared teppan (griddle), so cross-contact with wheat batter is unavoidable. No gluten-free preparation is documented.

mismatched.name: 京都 下町のお好み焼き 昌・べた焼きの専門店 (Kyoto Shitamachi no Okonomiyaki Masa (Be)
mismatched.text: Betayaki batter and toppings commonly include egg, and the menu features meat and pork-offal items (oil cas/aburakasu, beef, horumon). The single shared griddle cooks animal products, so vegan diners face heavy cross-contact. No vegan options are documented; confirm directly.

mismatched.name: べた焼き節ちゃん (Betayaki Setsu-chan)
mismatched.text: This is a betayaki/okonomiyaki shop where the batter is wheat-flour based. Betayaki and okonomiyaki are cooked on a shared teppan (iron griddle) alongside other wheat-containing dishes, so gluten cross-contact on the griddle is effectively unavoidable. No gluten-free menu or preparation is documented. This restaurant should be treated as not celiac-safe.

mismatched.name: 嘗〜miso〜 (Sho ~miso~)
mismatched.text: The menu features 生麩 (nama-fu / fresh wheat gluten) dengaku, which is essentially pure wheat gluten and must be strictly avoided by celiac diners; its presence in the kitchen also raises broader cross-contact concern.

mismatched.name: だるまときんぎょ (Daruma to Kingyo)
mismatched.text: There is a genuine focus on fresh, seasonal vegetable oden (daikon, tomato, avocado and more), so plant-forward diners without a strict animal-product or gluten restriction have appealing options to discuss with staff.

mismatched.name: 熟成豚 かわむら (Jukuseibuta Kawamura)
mismatched.text: The breading is wheat panko and the cutlets are deep-fried, meaning gluten is present throughout the core cooking process.

mismatched.name: 熟成豚 かわむら (Jukuseibuta Kawamura)
mismatched.text: Among the table condiments is a Yakushima ago-dashi soy sauce; most Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat, so it should be treated as containing gluten.

mismatched.name: 洋食 おがた (Yoshoku Ogata)
mismatched.text: There is no vegan or vegetarian offering documented. The menu centers on meat, seafood, eggs, and dairy (hamburger, fries, gratin, omurice), and even vegetable-forward items like the soup and salad are prepared in a kitchen dominated by animal-based stocks, butter, and demi-glace. Vegan cross-contact is effectively unavoidable here.

mismatched.name: 洋食の店　みしな (Yoshoku no Mise Mishina)
mismatched.text: This is a classic yoshoku fry restaurant built on wheat: crab cream croquettes, shrimp fry and fried sets use wheat-flour breading and batter, the signature beef stew is built on a roux-based two-week demi-glace, and the cream filling is flour-thickened. It is not celiac-safe and no gluten-free accommodation is documented.

mismatched.name: 呑龍 淀店 (Donryu Yodo-ten (Tonryu Yodo))
mismatched.text: Sauces and seasonings across the menu (fried rice, stir-fries, gyoza dipping, ramen broth, tenshinhan) are soy-sauce based, and standard Japanese soy sauce is brewed with wheat. No gluten-free soy sauce is documented.

mismatched.name: まるい食堂 (Marui Shokudo)
mismatched.text: Documented signature dishes are wheat-based ramen and udon in soy-sauce broths, with no indication of any gluten-free preparation or separate cooking surfaces.

mismatched.name: マルシン飯店 (Marushin Hanten)
mismatched.text: This is a wheat- and soy-heavy町中華 (Chinese diner): the core menu is gyoza (wheat dumpling wrappers), ramen (wheat noodles), tenshinhan and wok dishes built on soy sauce and wheat/soy-based seasonings. It is not celiac-safe, and cross-contamination risk is high.

mismatched.name: お数家いしかわ (Okazuya Ishikawa)
mismatched.text: The owners also run a sister tempura shop (Tempura Obanzai Ishikawa), and tempura batter is wheat-based; any fried items here carry a high risk of gluten and shared-oil cross-contact.

mismatched.name: お数家いしかわ (Okazuya Ishikawa)
mismatched.text: The menu is grounded in soy sauce, dashi and miso typical of Kyoto obanzai. Most Japanese soy sauce (and many dashi and seasoning blends) contains wheat, so soy-sauce-based dishes should be treated as containing wheat unless staff confirm otherwise.

mismatched.name: ろじうさぎ (Roji Usagi)
mismatched.text: Sweets such as the pudding, pudding parfait, pudding a la mode, and ice cream contain egg and dairy. One cake is noted as made without butter, but that does not make it vegan.

mismatched.name: 旬菜 いまり (Shunsai Imari)
mismatched.text: Soy sauce, miso and Saikyo miso marinades feature heavily (e.g. 銀鱈 西京漬け silver cod in Saikyo miso, 牛頬肉の赤味噌 braised beef cheek in red miso). Most Japanese soy sauce and many miso products contain wheat, so these dishes should be treated as containing gluten unless individually confirmed.

mismatched.name: 富小路 天ぷらまつ井 (Tominokoji Tempura Matsui)
mismatched.text: Tempura is fried low and light, and is noted as eating less heavy than typical tempura - though this does not change its gluten or animal-product content.

mismatched.name: 市川屋珈琲 (Ichikawaya Coffee)
mismatched.text: This is a coffee shop whose signature items are fruit sandwiches and egg sandwiches made on wheat bread, plus baked goods. There is no advertised gluten-free menu and no verified GF accommodation, so it is not celiac-safe. A diner with celiac disease should avoid the bread and baked items and confirm any other order directly with staff.

mismatched.name: 市川屋珈琲 (Ichikawaya Coffee)
mismatched.text: The menu centers on dairy (fresh cream, milk-based coffee drinks) and egg sandwiches, so vegan options are not advertised; vegan diners should ask staff what, if anything, can be prepared without animal products.

mismatched.name: 馬耳東風 (Baji Tofu)
mismatched.text: Even salt-only (塩) skewers, while reducing direct gluten exposure, cannot be considered celiac-safe given the shared grill surface and the pervasive use of soy sauce and tare nearby.

mismatched.name: 馬耳東風 (Baji Tofu)
mismatched.text: Yakitori glaze (tare) and soy-based seasonings are central to the menu, and most Japanese soy sauce and tare contain wheat. Tare skewers should be treated as containing gluten.

mismatched.name: 鳥さき (Torisaki)
mismatched.text: This is a single-counter yakitori omakase where every skewer is grilled on the same shared binchotan hearth. Both salt and tare (a wheat-containing soy-based sauce) skewers come off the same grill, so cross-contact is effectively unavoidable. Gluten-free cannot be assured and the meal is not celiac-safe.

mismatched.name: 鳥さき (Torisaki)
mismatched.text: The set is a fixed omakase that moves cut by cut through the bird and finishes with rice bowls such as soboro-don and oyakodon, leaving little room to remove gluten-containing components without unraveling the course.

mismatched.name: 鳥さき (Torisaki)
mismatched.text: Many skewers and the finishing rice bowls are seasoned with tare and soy-based sauces; standard Japanese soy sauce and yakitori tare contain wheat. The omakase leans on these soy- and dashi-based seasonings throughout.

mismatched.name: ヴィーガンラーメン ウズ キョウト (Vegan Ramen UZU KYOTO)
mismatched.text: Broth is a clean 12-hour kelp, shiitake and vegetable infusion with no fish or meat dashi.

mismatched.name: alt. coffee roasters（オルト コーヒー ロースターズ） (alt. coffee roasters)
mismatched.text: Staff speak English, making it easier for foreign visitors to discuss ingredients and allergies.

mismatched.name: 毘沙門堂 勝林寺 (Bishamondo Shourin-ji (Shourin Temple))
mismatched.text: Plant-based meals and matcha-with-sweets are prepared in a temple kitchen with no animal-protein cooking, so the risk of meat or fish cross-contact is inherently low.

mismatched.name: ブランジュリ ロワゾー・ブルー (Boulangerie L'Oiseau Bleu)
mismatched.text: The shop states all products are free from eggs, dairy and honey and are made to suit people with allergies and dietary restrictions, and the owner is described as very accommodating and willing to discuss ingredients.

mismatched.name: いただき繕 京都西陣店 (Itadakizen Kyoto (Itadaki Zen Kyoto Nish)
mismatched.text: Tofu steak can be prepared gluten-free, and some items have a gluten-free option, so GF-flexible diners have safe choices when staff are informed.

mismatched.name: Cacao∞Magic（カカオマジック） (Cacao Magic)
mismatched.text: Fully plant-based kitchen: all chocolate and sweets are made with no animal products whatsoever, dairy-free and egg-free, so the risk of animal cross-contact is minimal.

mismatched.name: 泉仙 大慈院店 (Izusen Daijiin-ten)
mismatched.text: Japanese soy sauce is standard in shojin seasoning and normally contains wheat; no wheat-free soy sauce is mentioned.

mismatched.name: 篩月（しげつ） (Tenryuji Shigetsu)
mismatched.text: Meals are reservation-based by phone (075-882-9725, 9:00–17:00), giving an opportunity to communicate allergies or dietary needs ahead of the visit; no formal allergy-handling program is published.

mismatched.name: 鴨川ベーカリー 京都本店 (KAMOGAWA BAKERY Kyoto Honten (Kamogawa B)
mismatched.text: Core breads use no butter, milk or eggs and rely on soy-milk butter and animal-free beet sugar, so plant-based options are clearly labeled and the menu is intentionally inclusive ('ONE TABLE').

mismatched.name: ソーシャル・キッチン（Social Kitchen） (Social Kitchen)
mismatched.text: The kitchen is not fully vegan and rotates among different operators by day, so animal ingredients may be used on the same equipment depending on who is cooking; confirm with the day's operator.

mismatched.name: 京のカレーうどん 味味香 祇園店 (Mimikou (Kyo no Curry Udon Mimikou, Gion)
mismatched.text: Primarily a wheat-udon shop; udon and ramen noodles are wheat, and battered tempura shares the kitchen, so high gluten cross-contact for any non-noodle order.

mismatched.name: 京大食堂 北部食堂 (Kyodai Shokudo Hokubu Shokudo (Kyoto Uni)
mismatched.text: Menu cards display nutritional balance and allergen information; staff recommend telling them about vegetarian/vegan needs and any allergies before choosing a dish.

mismatched.name: ブラウニーブレッドアンドベーグルズ (Browny Bread & Bagels)
mismatched.text: At least one variety is a soy-sauce mochi cheese bagel; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, and no wheat-free soy sauce is documented.

mismatched.name: ごはんぱん工房つぶつぶ (Gohan Pan Kobo Tsubutsubu)
mismatched.text: The facility also produces items containing eggs, dairy, peanuts, and honey, so there is cross-contamination risk for strictly plant-based diners.

mismatched.name: ごはんぱん工房つぶつぶ (Gohan Pan Kobo Tsubutsubu)
mismatched.text: The base bread is plant-based, using soy milk and rice oil instead of eggs and dairy; many items are free of eggs, dairy, and honey.

mismatched.name: インド食堂TADKA（タルカ） (Indo Shokudo TADKA (Tadka))
mismatched.text: The kitchen also prepares non-vegetarian dishes (especially at the TADKA2 dinner location), so shared cookware/cross-contact is possible; vegan diners should specify dairy-free and meat-free preparation.

mismatched.name: ゆば料理 東山ゆう豆 (Yuba Ryori Higashiyama Yuzu)
mismatched.text: The kitchen centers on house-made, additive-free yuba and a tofu-milk hot pot with Kyoto vegetables — plant-based, soy-forward dishes that form a strong vegetarian-friendly base if animal garnishes (egg, chicken, dashi) are omitted on request.

mismatched.name: 泉仙 嵯峨野店 (Izusen Sagano)
mismatched.text: The kitchen is a fully shojin (Buddhist vegetarian) operation serving no meat or fish, which greatly reduces the risk of animal cross-contact.

mismatched.name: 発酵食堂カモシカ (Hakkō Shokudō Kamoshika (Fermented Food )
mismatched.text: This is an omnivore kitchen: the signature set meal includes mackerel heshiko, pufferfish nukazuke, and fish-sauce konjac, so fish is handled in the same kitchen as plant-based dishes. White miso soup may use a fish (bonito) dashi — confirm it is kombu-only.

mismatched.name: ぴっぱら (Pippara)
mismatched.text: Freshly baked chapati (wheat) is part of the standard set and fried snacks use batter, so wheat is handled openly in the kitchen; no gluten-free accommodation is indicated.

mismatched.name: ぴっぱら (Pippara)
mismatched.text: This is an omnivore kitchen that also cooks fish/meat curries and dairy items (lassi, yogurt, paneer) in the same small space, so vegan dishes are prepared alongside animal products.
